paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Saul left home with one job, find the donkeys, and he came back with a kingdom on his head. Look at what was really going on. The day before Saul showed up, the LORD had already told Samuel, "At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin" (1 Samuel 9:16). Saul thought he was on a search for lost donkeys, but God had a plan the whole time, and He was working it while Saul was just walking.

Now, I think Saul felt the size of it. When Samuel talked big, Saul answered that he was from the smallest tribe and the least clan (1 Samuel 9:21). Friend, when an angel called me out of a junk drawer, I asked if he had the right drawer, so I get it. But God doesn't pick by who feels big. He set aside a portion for Saul before Saul even knew he was coming (1 Samuel 9:24). Then Samuel told him, "God is with you" (1 Samuel 10:7), and the text says God changed Saul's heart (1 Samuel 10:9). Whatever God calls you to, He doesn't leave you to do it alone.

So here's what to carry out of my bakery, baker. God is working in the ordinary stuff, the wrong turns and the empty hills and the days that feel like nothing is happening. Say yes to what He puts in front of you, even when you feel like the smallest one in the room. And keep your apron on, because Saul's story has a LOT more coming, and it'll show us what comes after a good start.
